description: Rewrites 'since <count> <duration-unit>' (a span) to 'for <count> <duration-unit>' for Vietlish 'trong / được N năm' transfer, where learners mark a duration span with the point-in-time preposition 'since'.
fp_risk_note: Low risk. Matches only 'since <number> <year|month|week|day|hour>'. A bare year ('since 2020'), a weekday ('since Monday'), and 'since last year / yesterday' never match. A trailing 'ago'/'old'/'back' (point-in-time or age: 'since 3 years ago', 'since 5 years old') and a leading 'ever' ('ever since 5 years', an idiom) are excluded by boundary guards so 'for ...' is never produced where it would be ungrammatical or change meaning. Sentence-initial 'Since' re-capitalizes to 'For'.

positive.notes: Numeric duration span mismarked with 'since' becomes 'for'.

positive.input: I studied English since two years
positive.expectedCorrection: I studied English for two years.
positive.notes: Spelled-out count is also covered by the whitelist.

positive.input: He has worked here since five months
positive.expectedCorrection: He has worked here for five months.
positive.notes: Present-perfect span with a months unit.

negative.notes: A bare year is a point in time — not a number + duration unit — so 'since' is correct.
'last year' has no numeric count so the duration pattern cannot match.

negative.input: I haven't seen him since Monday
negative.expectedCorrection: I haven't seen him since Monday.
negative.notes: A weekday is a point in time; 'since Monday' is correct and must be preserved.
'yesterday' is a point in time, not a number + duration unit.

negative.input: He was happy since 5 years old.
negative.expectedCorrection: He was happy since 5 years old.
negative.notes: Age expression 'since 5 years old' (= since age 5); 'for 5 years old' would be ungrammatical -> 'old' boundary guard abstains. (A4 regression lock.)

negative.input: I met him since 3 years ago.
negative.expectedCorrection: I met him since 3 years ago.
negative.notes: Point-in-time 'since N years ago'; 'for N years ago' is never valid -> 'ago' boundary guard abstains. (A4 regression lock.)

negative.input: We have been friends ever since 5 years.
negative.expectedCorrection: We have been friends ever since 5 years.
negative.notes: 'ever since' is an idiom; splitting it ('ever for 5 years') is nonsense -> leading 'ever' lookbehind abstains. (A4 regression lock.)
